ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and proposed beneficial owners against (i) the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, (ii) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) Consolidated List, (iii) the US OFAC SDN List, (iv) the Bermuda domestic Sanctions List, and (v) global PEP/adverse-media databases (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance). Any PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media hit triggers enhanced due diligence and escalation to the BMA-supervised compliance officer; ongoing monitoring is required for the life of the entity in line with FATF Recommendations and Bermuda AML/CFT guidance. Positive PEP status alone does not prohibit incorporation but requires source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies eServices Portal (Companies e-Services, roc.gov.bm)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in English using the Roman alphabet; only English letters, numerals and permitted punctuation are accepted, with no diacritics or non-Roman script. The name of a Bermuda Exempted Company must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd' as its last word to denote limited liability. A foreign-language trading name or transliteration may be used commercially outside Bermuda, but the registered legal name remains the English statutory name and must be used identically in all constitutional documents, the register and filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may (a) file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, attaching evidence of prior use, written consent from any entity with a similar or conflicting name, and the original payment receipt; (b) if reconsideration is denied, lodge an administrative appeal to the Minister of Finance or Financial Secretary within 30 calendar days pursuant to the Companies Act 1981; or (c) apply to the Supreme Court of Bermuda for judicial review. Alternatively, the applicant may refile a revised name clearance application on the eServices portal with a new name and the applicable statutory fee. Extension of a valid name reservation may be requested in writing before expiry, subject to the Registrar's published fee schedule and availability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the statutory registered office. Section 87 of the Companies Act 1981 requires the exempted company to maintain a continuous physical registered office in Bermuda at which legal process and official notices may be served; a virtual office without physical premises fails this requirement. The registered office may lawfully be the licensed registered agent's physical address in Bermuda, with full administrative back-office functions delegated to that agent. The ghost kitchen and virtual brand operations themselves will be conducted through a UK operating subsidiary, with the Bermuda Exempted Company retaining board oversight, trademark/licensing, and treasury functions; any UK management and control may render the company UK tax resident, which must be disclosed and managed through proper substance and intercompany arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified as low-to-moderate: approximately 15-20% annual probability of a desk-based compliance or economic substance review by the Registrar or the Economic Substance Secretariat, and approximately 5-10% probability of a physical on-site inspection, primarily triggered by claims of UK tax residence, incomplete economic substance filings, adverse media, or unexplained fund flows. Unannounced physical visits are possible but are normally targeted at high-risk filers rather than standard low-risk delivery-only catering structures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981 (as amended): ss. 4–6 (incorporation), s. 14 (exempted companies), s. 14A (non-resident ownership), First Schedule (Memorandum and Bye-laws); Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966; Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2018; Economic Substance Act 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Department of Registrar General, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (Hamilton, Bermuda).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws filed with the Registrar of Companies, supported by Application for Exemption and Statement of First Directors/Secretary; Certificate of Incorporation issued upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; standard subscription is one (1) Ordinary Share of BMD 1.00 (USD 1.00) fully paid in cash. No escrow or capital deposit rules apply; the register of members must be maintained at the Bermuda registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber to these Bye-laws subscribe for and be allotted one (1) Ordinary Share of par value BMD 1.00 at par, payable in full in lawful money. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [Bermuda Registered Office Address], and Marsh Lane Corporate Services Ltd. be appointed registered agent and corporate secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that John A. Smith be and hereby is appointed Director, President and Treasurer, and Jane B. Doe be appointed Director and Secretary, each to serve until replaced by the Board. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers named above are authorized to execute all incorporation, banking, licensing, and employment documents to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (online corporate registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Bermuda Companies Registry portal to confirm availability and legal acceptability. Submit a name reservation application ensuring the name ends with 'Limited' and does not conflict with existing Bermuda entities or regulated financial names. Obtain the name clearance letter before preparing constitutional documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for similarity, resubmit with two alternative names and, where possible, a letter of consent from the conflicting entity; appeal a refusal to the Registrar within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Notary Public and appointing subscriber / licensed corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association (objects clause and share capital) and the Bye-laws (governance, share rights, board powers). Execute the subscriber page in the presence of a Bermuda notary, and obtain the registered agent's written acceptance of appointment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar later queries the objects or capital clause, amend by written resolution, re-execute before a notary, and resubmit with a corrected date and signature page.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Registry General, Hamilton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws, Application for Exempted Company Status, Statement of First Directors/Secretary, Notice of Registered Office, and the statutory registration fee of BMD 1,230. Receive the Certificate of Incorporation on approval.
required_dossiers: Statement of First Directors and Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries incomplete forms or fees, rectify within 7 business days through the filing agent; failure triggers re-filing with incremental penalty, so monitor the portal daily.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Minister of Finance (Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a formal application with the Minister of Finance for a Tax Exemption Certificate confirming no Bermuda income, capital, dividend, or withholding taxes until 31 March 2035 (as extended). Demonstrate that the company is not beneficially owned by Bermuda residents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Minister requests supplementary ownership evidence, file a restated shareholder structure chart and notarized declarations; respond within the 21-day query window to avoid cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Registered Office, Registered Agent, and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (register of agents and registered offices)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formalize the licensed Bermuda registered office and registered agent (corporate services firm) that will hold the statutory records. Execute the first board resolution appointing initial directors and officers, and file any required officer details with the Registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate services provider rejects the client file, promptly complete enhanced due diligence on ultimate beneficial owners and resubmit the acceptance letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Register and Annual Validation Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Beneficial Ownership Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the Beneficial Ownership Register under the Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2018 and file the required beneficial ownership data with the Registrar. Concurrently prepare the annual validation filing (due before 31 January each year) and assess economic substance reporting obligations under the Economic Substance Act 2018.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late filing penalties apply, use the 30-day grace window, pay the BMD 500-plus tiered penalty, and correct the register promptly; amend the register whenever shareholdings change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK Establishment Registration and Pre-Operating Food Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: UK Companies House and the relevant London Borough Council Environmental Health Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Bermuda Exempted Company's UK operational branch as an 'UK establishment' of an overseas company under the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009 (Form OS IN01) at Companies House. Then submit Food Business Registration for the dark kitchen premises to the local council under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and obtain planning use approval for a delivery-only kitchen.
required_dossiers: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation with English translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the council requires a pre-opening hygiene inspection, schedule within 28 days, remedy critical hygiene and ventilation deficiencies, and re-submit for registration before first food service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: UK Food Standards Agency (FSA) in conjunction with the local London Borough Council Environmental Health Service for the UK operating branch of the Bermuda Exempted Company.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013, together with Sui Generis planning consent for a delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: UK Environment Agency in coordination with the regional water authority (e.g., Thames Water Utilities) for trade effluent consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Low Tier (Exempt from Full EIA) — single-site batch food preparation with under 1,000 covers per day; triggers Environmental Health pre-opening inspection, Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011 waste carrier registration, and no full Environmental Impact Assessment development consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade effluent: oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L via approved grease interceptor, pH 6–10, COD below 1,000 mg/L. Ventilation and VOCs: odour-neutral extraction stack discharging not less than 1 m above roof level, zero visible smoke, and particulate filtration compliant with the Clean Air Act 1993. Waste handling: licensed food-waste carrier collections, zero untreated discharge to drains except screened wash-water. Refrigerants: F-gas registration for all HVAC/R equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Risk Assessment and fire safety compliance certificate under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, with London Fire Brigade approval of the emergency plan; building control structural load clearance and commercial kitchen gas installation certification (Gas Safe Register); Health and Safety Executive workplace clearance plus local council food hygiene inspection under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 before commissioning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bermuda Ministry of Finance (Office of the Tax Commissioner) and the Bermuda Registrar of Companies; official government portal is https://www.gov.bm. Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory with a separate tax administration from HMRC; UK taxes do not automatically apply in Bermuda.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company has no Bermudian corporate income-tax registration requirement and no VAT/TIN identification obligation. The statutory identifier is the company number issued by the Registrar of Companies upon incorporation under the Companies Act 1981. A foreign-owned entity forms the company through a licensed registered agent, files its memorandum of association, articles of association and required declarations, receives the Certificate of Incorporation, then obtains the Exempted Company approvals/permit through the Ministry of Finance where required. If the company later employs individuals physically present in Bermuda, it must separately register as an employer for payroll tax with the Office of the Tax Commissioner and obtain a payroll tax account number. No general TIN is issued solely for tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No local Bermudian check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists. The 'Exempted Company' status is obtained through company registration, not as a tax election. For owners subject to U.S. federal tax, the Bermuda entity may independently file IRS Form 8832 to elect classification as a corporation, partnership, or disregarded entity under the U.S. check-the-box regime, but this filing has no effect on Bermudian tax status. Bermuda has no participation-exemption, group-election, or hybrid-mismatch rules for direct tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — Bermuda does not operate VAT, GST, or sales tax. No turnover threshold triggers indirect-tax registration. Imported physical goods may be subject to customs duty under the Customs Tariff Act 2008, and certain limited transaction taxes such as stamp duty and land tax may apply, but these are not turnover-based registration regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Bermuda has no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance API, digital stamping, or government authorization requirement for commercial invoices. Cloud kitchen delivery platform invoicing can be issued through ordinary accounting or billing software without prior tax-authority validation. Records must be kept according to the Companies Act 1981 and the Exchange Control Act 1972 where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Because Bermuda imposes no VAT, GST, or sales tax, there is no export zero-rating claim and no refund mechanism in Bermuda. Deliveries of goods or services from Bermuda to the United Kingdom, European Union, or other destination jurisdictions will instead be subject to the indirect tax regime of the destination jurisdiction, if any. Bermuda does not tax exports and does not provide a VAT export refund.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not required for any Bermuda VAT zero-rating claim, as no such claim exists.
If physical goods depart Bermuda, Bermuda Customs may request an Export Declaration or Shipping Bill under the Customs Act 2010 for control and duty-relief purposes.
Commercial Invoice used for customs valuation and export clearance.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export movement from Bermuda.
Packing List, where applicable for physical consignments.
Inward Remittance Certificate or payment proof, required only if a foreign tax authority requires evidence of consideration received; Bermuda itself does not impose this condition.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Since Bermuda has no VAT/GST, there is no Bermudian export zero-rating refund or clawback mechanism. Foreign VAT authorities may nevertheless scrutinize any export-based zero-rating or refund claimed by an associated UK/EU entity; fraudulent documentation can trigger retrospective VAT clawback plus interest and penalties in that foreign jurisdiction. Within Bermuda, false customs declarations, undervaluation, or mis-description of exported goods are punishable under the Customs Act 2010 by forfeiture, monetary penalties up to the statutory limit, and imprisonment. False statements or omissions in Economic Substance Act declarations can result in civil penalties, distraint, and in serious cases strike-off or winding up of the Bermudian entity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA), acting under the Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 and the Exchange Control Act 1972, supplemented by the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2018.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermuda dollar (BMD) maintains a statutory 1:1 peg with the USD, administered by the BMA. Bermuda operates a fully liberalised exchange control regime for exempted companies: both current account and capital account transactions are freely convertible, with no restrictions on dividend distributions, profit repatriation, intercompany loans, or liquidation proceeds. Non-resident owned exempted companies holding a BMA Certificate of Exemption receive automatic general permission for foreign currency accounts, capital injections, and outward remittances. Practical remittance hurdles are limited to AML/KYC documentary thresholds rather than balance-of-payments controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio in Bermuda. A Bermuda Exempted Company deriving revenue from ghost kitchen delivery platforms (UberEats, DoorDash) may retain USD, GBP, EUR, or any freely convertible currency in its BMA-licensed bank accounts indefinitely. The BMA, however, requires reporting of any single inbound/outbound payment exceeding BMD 100,000 (or equivalent) under its large-value transaction reporting obligations, and all cross-border flows must be supported by underlying trade or capital documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited
The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, with strict legal constraints. Bermuda does not recognise the UK or EU EMI passporting regime; an offshore digital EMI is not licensed by the BMA to open deposit accounts for a Bermuda exempted company unless it holds a restricted banking licence under the Banks and Deposit Companies Act 1999. In practice, UK FCA-regulated EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Airwallex) may accept a Bermuda exempted company as a client solely as a payment service provider, subject to their own correspondent banking policy. These rails are viable for small GBP/EUR disbursements but are inadequate for primary treasury operations: they frequently reject UberEats/DoorDash aggregated payout wiring, and they lack access to the BMD/USD local clearing. The EMI channel should be limited to a secondary operational buffer, never the capital escrow facility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted at Butterfield, HSBC, and Clarien for Bermuda exempted companies, with no statutory in-person appearance requirement. The BMA's customer due diligence rules mandate 'adequate verification' of each director and signatory, which the banks satisfy through: (i) notarised passport copies, (ii) acceptable proof of residential address issued within the last three months, (iii) a professional or bank reference from the BMA-licensed corporate services provider acting as registered agent, and (iv) a live video identification interview recorded for audit retention. In exceptional cases, such as a director residing in a jurisdiction on the FATF grey list or a UBO presenting a complex trust structure, Butterfield or HSBC may require an in-branch interview (Hamilton or Cayman) as a discretionary risk mitigation measure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity across multiple virtual brand entities stacking revenue into a single treasury account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract of the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register (under the Companies and Limited Liability Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2018), full organisational chart, UBO passports and residential addresses, and clear written source-of-wealth narratives for each individual owning more than 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated marketplace payout pattern from UberEats and DoorDash classified as unverifiable trade receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant agreements with UberEats and DoorDash, monthly settlement statements from the platforms, reconciliations of the aggregated payout logs to the entity's sales ledger, and an independent third-party AML audit opinion confirming the platform payouts originate from regulated acquiring banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border intercompany funding from the UK parent triggering FATCA/CRS misclassification risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda tax residency certificate issued by the BMA, CRS self-certification form under the OECD Common Reporting Standard, IRS FATCA registration acknowledgment, and a certified copy of the intercompany loan or equity injection resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US/EEA nexus via delivery platform payouts causing sanctions screening flags on payment routing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, UN, EU, and UK consolidated sanctions list screening results for all directors and UBOs, a geographic nexus analysis of the ghost kitchen locations, and evidence that no sanctioned counterparty appears in the top-vendor list of the virtual brand supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classified as 'shell risk' due to minimal local economic substance in Bermuda
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BMA economic substance declaration confirming the entity is a non-resident pure equity holding or IP-holding vehicle exempt from substance requirements, or alternatively a substance report showing board meetings, registered office records, and statutory filings demonstrating compliance with the International Business Companies regime.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the UK parent are executed via SWIFT MT103 from a UK bank to the Bermuda entity's USD operational or escrow account through the bank's New York correspondent (CHIPS). Instructions must state purpose code 'Equity Injection - Foreign Direct Investment' (IMF BOP code EQ/5130), reference the Bermuda Exchange Control general permission granted to exempted companies, and attach the executed board resolution authorising share issuance. No BMD conversion occurs given the 1:1 USD peg. For marketplace payouts (UberEats/DoorDash), inbound routing arrives as aggregated ACH or Fedwire settlements from the platform's US operating entity; these must be pre-notified to the Bermuda bank with the platform merchant agreement and a statement of payout period to satisfy large-value reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for discrete supplier payments (kitchen equipment, food-grade packaging, technology licensing) cleared via CHIPS in New York for USD or via target2 for EUR. For high-value capital imports from Asia (e.g., commercial cooking suites), an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP600) is preferred, issued by the Bermuda bank through a London or New York confirming bank; presentation documents must be unicorporated under the BMD/USD peg. Dividend and royalty distributions to the UK parent are routed via MT103 with purpose code 'Dividend Distribution', accompanied by audited financial statements and the BMA dividend approval letter, cleared via CHIPS in USD with conversion into GBP at the receiving UK bank, or alternatively via the UK Faster Payments Service using the EMI buffer for small sub-USD 10,000 payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Natural BMD/USD hedge pursuant to the statutory 1:1 peg, eliminating all USD/BMD conversion risk
Outright deliverable forwards in USD/GBP (tenors up to 12 months) for GBP-denominated UK supplier and payroll obligations
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/GBP for floating rate exposure arising from UK intercompany loans where no UK physical clearing relationship exists
Cross-currency swaps between USD and GBP for medium-term intercompany funding harmonisation
Zero-cost collars (capped options) on USD/GBP for operational margin protection of the ghost kitchen virtual brands

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return accompanied by Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues monthly administrative penalties; continued default for approximately 12 months exposes the exempted company to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies - Beneficial Ownership Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the incorporation anniversary rule; beneficial ownership changes arising from share transfers must be reported within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence subject to BMD fines and compliance orders; persistent non-compliance may restrict the company's operations and affect the directors' good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies - Economic Substance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the relevant financial year (30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing attracts escalating fixed penalties and may trigger exchange of information with HM Revenue & Customs under Bermuda's economic substance framework.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies to publicly listed, licensed, permit and regulated exempted companies. A private exempted company may apply to the Registrar for audit exemption if it has 20 or fewer shareholders, has not made a public offering and does not conduct Bermuda-regulated business; shareholders holding at least 10% may require audited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda does not prescribe a local GAAP; financial statements are prepared under IFRS or US GAAP as adopted by the board and must give a true and fair view.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Act 2018 requires the exempted company to maintain a beneficial-ownership register and file an annual confirmation with the Registrar. Any share-transfer event changing beneficial ownership must be reported within 14 days; the company secretary must contemporaneously update the register and re-confirm the UBO particulars on the next annual confirmation cycle.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% general Bermuda corporate income tax for Exempted Companies; 15% Bermuda Corporate Income Tax (CIT) applies exclusively to in-scope MNE groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750M in at least two of the four preceding fiscal years (Pillar Two aligned, effective for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2025).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax Exemption Certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 grants statutory protection from future Bermuda income/capital taxes until 31 March 2035; no capital gains tax, no sales tax, no stamp duty on shares; employer payroll tax (4.75%-10.25%) and social insurance remain the only labor-related charges; out-of-scope SMEs enjoy an effective rate of 0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for in-scope CIT groups (GloBE-compliant loss credit carryforward, no carryback); not applicable (0%) for out-of-scope exempted companies

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (ESD / ESR Form) — filed electronically through the Bermuda Registrar of Companies Integrated Registry System (e-Registry / BFRS portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the end of the entity's financial period (a 31 December year-end entity must file by 30 June of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Bermuda registration number, registered office address, financial period start/end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned Exempted Company must confirm the registered office is maintained at a licensed Bermuda service provider

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISIC classification of activity and box to mark whether the company is a Non-Relevant Entity (NRE) or Relevant Activity (RA) entity; ghost kitchen food operations are NRE, but brand-IP holding triggers RA 'Intellectual Property Business'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare ISIC 5610 (food service) as NRE; if trademarks of virtual brands are held in Bermuda, IP business rules apply and the CIGA test (core income-generating activity in Bermuda) must be evidenced

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C: Economic Substance Test (RA entities only)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm CIGA conducted in Bermuda, adequate physical presence, employees, expenditure, and board management in Bermuda
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For NRE entities, leave blank and file nil; in-scope IP entities must produce board minutes and employment records demonstrating Bermuda substance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Initial penalty BMD 10,000 plus BMD 10,000 per month of continued non-compliance; misdeclaration or false information attracts a fine of up to BMD 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Annual Return and Annual Fee Filing — e-Registry portal of the Registrar of Companies
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the end of the entity's financial year (the standard Bermuda deadline is 31 January for calendar-year entities under the current Registrar practice, but the legal requirement is 6 months post-period-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm current Bermuda registered office and resident agent/secretary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempted company must maintain a Bermuda-registered office and normally a resident secretary; provide licensed corporate service provider details

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List all directors, officers, and shareholder details; confirm minimum of two directors (individuals) and one shareholder
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign residents may serve as directors, but the Board must meet quorum requirements and minutes should evidence Bermuda management for UK-residency avoidance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Issued Share Capital and Beneficial Ownership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare issued share capital and beneficial ownership details for the Bermuda BO Register (under the Companies and Partnership (Economic Substance) and (Beneficial Ownership) legislation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners must be identified to the BO agent; nil returns are not permitted where BO exists

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine BMD 200 plus BMD 100 per day up to a maximum; continued default can lead to deregistration and director disqualification

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: UK Corporate Tax Return (CT600) and supplementary computations — HMRC via commercial software or HMRC online (mandatory if a UK permanent establishment (PE) or UK tax residence risk arises; Ghost kitchen delivery operations in the UK will almost certainly create a UK PE)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporation tax return filing due 12 months after the end of the accounting period; corporation tax payment due 9 months and 1 day after period end (19%/25% rates for 2024 onwards; 25% main rate for profits above GBP 250,000, 19% small profits rate below GBP 50,000)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the company's tax residence status; a Bermuda Exempted Company whose central management and control is exercised in the UK is UK-resident regardless of Bermuda incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bermuda entity acting as head office should retain substantive board decision-making in Bermuda; otherwise declare UK residence and pay UK CT on global profits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CT600 Box 11 / 12: Trading and Non-Trading Profits (PE Computation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: UK-source trading profits attributable to the UK delivery kitchen PE; reconcile with Bermuda books and transfer pricing records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion profits using OECD authorized OECD Approach (AOA) for PEs; the Bermuda PE return should claim the UK-Bermuda Double Taxation Arrangement 2019 credit to avoid double taxation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CT600 Box 30 / related schedules: Intra-Group Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose transactions with the Bermuda parent/holding entity, including brand royalty payments, management fees, and intercompany loans
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Arm's length prices must be supported by a UK transfer pricing report; HMRC can adjust profits and impose penalties if documentation is absent

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty GBP 100 to GBP 1,000 escalating to tax-geared penalties above 6 months; late payment interest at Bank of England base rate plus 2.5%; deliberate inaccuracy penalty up to 100% of the tax, plus GBP 300 per failed quarterly (PAYE) return if employee payroll is present

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% Bermuda withholding tax on dividends paid by a Bermuda Exempted Company; 0% UK withholding tax on dividends paid by UK companies (UK dividends are always paid gross); therefore, profit repatriation from the UK PE to the Bermuda parent and onward to ultimate investors carries zero statutory dividend withholding in both jurisdictions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The UK-Bermuda Double Taxation Arrangement (signed 30 April 2019, effective 1 January 2020) is limited and contains NO dividends article; treaty relief is therefore not required for dividends. Protocol for any available relief (e.g., business profits PE article): (1) obtain Bermuda Tax Exemption Certificate and annual Bermuda tax residence letter; (2) claim UK foreign tax credit using Form DT / FTCR on the CT600 for Bermuda tax paid (if any); (3) retain UK and Bermuda corporate records evidencing no dual residence; (4) file HMRC Form A1/DT application only where the limited arrangement is invoked for shipping/air transport or PE profits; (5) for all other income, rely on domestic exemptions (e.g., UK s.931A CTA 2009 dividend exemption). TRC submission generally requires a certified copy issued by the Bermuda Ministry of Finance within 6 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: UK outbound: 20% WHT on UK-source royalties and 20% WHT on UK-source interest paid to a Bermuda recipient; no treaty reduction exists under the UK-Bermuda DTA because the arrangement lacks royalty/interest articles. Bermuda outbound: 0% WHT on royalties and interest paid by the Bermuda company. Practical guidance: brand royalty flows from the UK operating entity to the Bermuda IP holder will suffer 20% UK WHT unless the royalty is economically connected to a UK PE (then taxed as trade income) or an exemption such as the 'UK company recipient' or 'UK PE' exceptions under CTA 2010 s.908 / s.908A applies; interest on intercompany debt is taxable in the UK at 20% unless the beneficial owner is a UK bank or qualifying UK resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Bermuda (CIT regime): in-scope CIT groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750M must prepare and file a Master File and Local File aligned to the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; out-of-scope exempted companies have no Bermuda statutory TP return. UK side (UK PE of the Bermuda company): HMRC TP documentation (Local File) is mandatory when the group is 'large' — group turnover exceeds GBP 200M — and cross-border controlled transactions with the Bermuda head office exceed GBP 1M for goods or GBP 500K for services, intangibles, or financing; penalties for failure to keep contemporaneous documentation are up to GBP 50,000 per document category.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) — preferred for brand royalties and delivery platform services
Resale Price Method — used for the UK kitchen's buy-in of food ingredients from related sources
Cost Plus Method — appropriate for the UK PE's contract food-preparation and delivery fulfillment functions
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) — most practical for routine ghost kitchen operations using UK operating margin benchmarks
Profit Split Method — reserved for integrated virtual-brand IP value chains with unique intangibles
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Bermuda Economic Substance Regulations 2018 (as amended) apply; 'Intellectual Property Business' and certain other relevant activities require core income-generating activities (CIGA), physical presence, employees, and expenditure in Bermuda. Ghost kitchen foodservice (ISIC 5610) is NOT a listed relevant activity and is treated as a Non-Relevant Entity (NRE), requiring only a nil ESD. However, if the virtual-brand trademarks, delivery-app customer databases, or proprietary recipes are held in the Bermuda entity, the activity becomes an IP Business subject to full ESR substance testing in Bermuda; failure attracts the BMD 10,000/month penalties. Simultaneously, the UK will scrutinize whether the Bermuda entity has practical control over the IP (HMRC may reallocate profits under CTA 2009 Pt 4 or apply the Diverted Profits Tax if the Bermuda IP structure has no real commercial substance).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: UK Tax Residence Mismanagement (Central Management and Control)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Bermuda Exempted Company's directors hold board meetings in the UK, UK-based managers make day-to-day operational and strategic decisions for the ghost kitchen, and the Bermuda registered office acts only as postal agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC treats the company as UK-resident and assesses 25% UK corporation tax on worldwide profits; back taxes plus interest (base rate + 2.5%); penalties for failure to notify (up to 100% of tax) and for erroneous CT600 returns (up to 100%); additional assessment period can extend 20 years for deliberate conduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed under CTA 2010 s.217 for tax owed when the company is expected to get into serious difficulties; fraudulent evasion of income tax carries up to 7 years' imprisonment under TMA 1970 s.106A; HMRC can obtain freezing orders, leave-to-enter restrictions, and director disqualification orders (up to 15 years)

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bermuda Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false Economic Substance Declaration claiming Non-Relevant Entity status while material brand IP is held in Bermuda, or holding board meetings and CIGA outside Bermuda without proper delegation; deriving profits from UK delivery operations without any Bermuda presence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Bermuda Minister may impose a penalty of BMD 10,000 plus BMD 10,000 for each month the failure continues; false declarations attract a fine of BMD 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; the company may be struck off the register and its assets revert to the Crown
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the exempted company can be criminally prosecuted for knowingly permitting a false statement; in addition, the UK may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors/corporate-service-provider associates jointly liable for diverted profits tax and UK VAT where the Bermuda entity is a mere façade

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Diverted Profits Tax (DPT) on Artificial Bermuda Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Arrangements where the Bermuda parent lacks economic substance and its role is to siphon profits from the UK ghost kitchen via excessive royalties or by booking delivery-platform revenues outside the UK; HMRC may issue a DPT notice if it considers the 'avoided PE' or 'insufficient economic substance' conditions are met
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 25% DPT rate on diverted profits, no deduction for the royalty paid; DPT must be paid within 30 days of the notice; interest accrues; HMRC may also open a corporate tax enquiry and impose penalties of up to double the tax for deliberately concealed arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: HMRC can charge a designated director under s.23 FA 2015 (DPT) for the penalty where the company is insolvent and the director materially contributed to the penalty condition; travel bans (HMRC 'conduct notices') and disqualification as a UK director (CDDA 1986) may apply; in serious cases, cheating the public revenue is an indictable offence with a maximum life sentence

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: UK VAT and Delivery Platform Compliance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register for UK VAT once taxable turnover from UberEats/DoorDash and on-site hot-food sales exceeds GBP 90,000; under-declaring hot-food supplies (standard-rated 20%) as cold-food (zero-rated); issuing incorrect invoices for delivery platform fees; operating under the Bermuda entity while the actual UK kitchen is a taxable establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT civil penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded (for deliberate concealment); surcharge up to 15% on late-paid VAT; assessment can cover the previous 4 years (deliberate: 20 years); HMRC can wind up the company for unpaid VAT; third-party liability can extend to platform operators in some circumstances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in VAT evasion commit the criminal offence of fraudulent evasion of VAT under VATA 1994 s.72, punishable by imprisonment up to 7 years and unlimited fines; personal guarantees and joint-and-several liability under Finance Act 2009 Sch 46 (Senior Accounting Officer regime) for large companies; travel restrictions and asset seizure through 'Unexplained Wealth Orders' (UWOs) in high-value cases
